text:
maya: Heads up — I'm seeing a cluster of alerts for prom remote_write queue depth in eu-west-1 (~10k). Scrapers are reporting connection resets to our Cortex endpoints and a bunch of 5xx in the prom logs. Did anyone touch relabel configs or scrape timeouts recently?

opsbot: ALERT: prom-remote-write-queue-high (eu-west-1) triggered for prom-scraper-3; queue_depth=10123, p95_write_latency=8.2s :rotating_light:

liam: On it. Can you paste the last 200 lines of prom logs from prom-scraper-3?

maya: Sure — snippet from prom-scraper-3 logs:
```
2026-03-17T14:02:11Z prom_scrape_manager remote_write POST https://cortex-eu-west.internal/api/prom/push 502 Bad Gateway
2026-03-17T14:02:13Z prom_scrape_manager remote_write send failed write timeout: write tcp 10.0.0.12:45123->10.0.0.7:443: write: broken pipe
2026-03-17T14:02:15Z prom_scrape_manager remote_write http2: server closed idle connection
2026-03-17T14:02:18Z prom_scrape_manager dropped samples: send timeout (backend slow)
2026-03-17T14:03:00Z prom_scrape_manager remote_write POST ... 503 Service Unavailable
```

priya: I merged a relabel PR ~35m ago that started copying pod labels into a new label called `pod_meta`. It was supposed to be scoped but I may have missed an exclude. That could cause a cardinality spike if we ended up attaching git SHAs/env to metrics.

jordan: This is the relabel stanza I added to the PR review comments (looks suspicious):
```
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_git_sha]
    target_label: pod_meta_git_sha
  - action: replace
    source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_branch]
    target_label: pod_meta_branch
```
If those labels are present for many pods we blow up series cardinality.

liam: Quick mitigation — revert that relabel PR or add a `action: drop` rule to prevent `pod_meta_*` from being sent for ephemeral pods. Also consider increasing `remote_write` timeout and write buffer limits in eu-west while we heal.

priya: Rolling back now. Reverted the relabel commit and pushed a rollback PR.

opsbot: RESOLVED: prom-remote-write-queue-high (eu-west-1) — alert cleared for prom-scraper-3. queue_depth fell to 1200; p95_write_latency 1.3s :white_check_mark:

maya: Nice. Queue cleared but we still saw elevated p95 for a few minutes. Action items: 1) add relabel unit test to CI that simulates label explosion 2) add a runbook step to bump remote_write `send_timeout` to 30s in eu-west under overload 3) tune alert to use sustained window (5m->10m) for this specific queue alert to reduce noise.

liam: Filed INF-3421 for postmortem + runbook. Also proposing a CI job to compute expected cardinality delta for relabel PRs using a small sampled scrape dataset.

jordan: FYI I noticed the GPU node-autoscaler was spawning a lot of ephemeral diagnostic pods around the same time which added a noisy label `diag_run_id`. I'll patch node-exporter relabel rules to drop `diag_run_id` from metrics.

maya: Thanks all. Let's keep an eye on eu-west for the next 2h and correlate with k8s pod churn dashboards. If anything re-trips, escalate to oncall-sre.
